output.brief:
The Kestria buffering problem is not the new CDN. Session data for 12–25 October shows that only the smart-TV app version 5.2 stalls badly: about 5.9% of viewing time, against 0.6–0.7% for every other client. Those other clients are served by Tessaline too, and the gap is the same on all three ISPs. The 5.2 release went live on 9 October, the same day as the cutover, which is why the two were confused. Stalls were already high before the handball launch and did not rise on match nights, so handball is not the cause. I'm about 90% sure the 5.2 app is the cause.

Do not send the breach notice, withhold fees or move traffic back to Corvane. That would punish the wrong party and leave the problem in place. Do not mute the rebuffering alert either.

Next steps: revert the 5.2 adaptive-streaming behaviour to the 5.1 settings in Kestria and hold the wider rollout until it is fixed. Then check that rebuffering falls. Add app-version and device breakdowns to the dashboard; the current rebuild is about six weeks away, so ask for an interim fix.

Hold off on any win-back offer. The cancellation rise coincides with the 1 October price rise, and the exit survey has no option for streaming quality, so buffering as the cause is unproven.
